summary: This sermon challenges Christians to follow Jesus' example of having 'no reputation' by prioritizing vulnerability and authenticity over protecting their image. The preacher argues that the church's self-righteousness and reputation-management often becomes the biggest stumbling block preventing the world from seeing Jesus, and calls for confession, repentance, and genuine community accountability instead.
key_points: The church can either further God's kingdom or be its biggest stumbling block
Jesus made himself of no reputation, taking the form of a servant
Protecting our reputation leads to hiding sin and self-righteous hypocrisy
We should build Jesus' reputation, not our own or our church's
Authentic community requires vulnerability, confession, and mutual accountability
big_idea: Christians must lay aside concern for their own reputation and embrace vulnerability and confession, following Jesus who made himself of no reputation, so the world sees Christ rather than self-righteous stumbling blocks.
title: Poured Out: Seat-Belt Christians
